item.title: Late INT by Thomas Georgeadis preserves Class AA semifinal win for Saratoga Springs football
item.description: Saratoga Springs quarterback Bobby Morris looks for a receiver during the Section 2 Class AA semifinals against Shaker on Friday in Saratoga Springs. (Jim Franco/Times Union) SARATOGA SPRINGS - During an evening that featured 871 yards of offense and 77 points, defense ultimately won out for the Saratoga Springs football team. Shaker found itself deep in Blue Streaks' territory during the final minute of Friday's thrilling Section 2 Class AA semifinal showdown ,trailing by seven points. But, Saratoga junior linebacker Thomas Georgeadis put an end to Shaker's comeback aspirations when he intercepted a pass to help preserve a wild 42-35 victory over the Blue Bison. These two teams met in Week 5 at Saratoga Springs and the Blue Streaks easily prevailed 42-20 in a game that was not remotely as close as the final score would indicate. Friday night, Shaker fell behind twice by 21 points and refused to go away in a game where the Blue Bison outgained Saratoga Springs by 145 yards. "That was a great game by Shaker. They definitely did a good job. The came with a good game plan and their kids were very physical," Saratoga Springs coach Eric Hayden said. "Hats off to them. We found a way to win and that is all that matters." "I am so happy for the team," Saratoga Springs senior quarterback Bobby Morris said. "We graduated a lot of guys from last year's team (that beat CBA 14-13 for the title), but the new guys we have stepped up into new roles and done a hell of a job. I am really proud of them for that. We've got a big opponent next week coming off a big win. This wasn't the Super Bowl. We are happy, but we're not satisfied." The victory by Saratoga Springs (9-1 overall), winners of the 2025 sectional title, sends them back to the Super Bowl for a rematch against top-seeded Christian Brothers Academy (10-0) Nov. 14 at Colonie High School. Saratoga Springs led 28-14 at halftime and expanded the lead to 35-14 in the third quarter. "A lot of times this season, our offense has not performed to its potential," Morris said. "Defensively, they've had our backs. This game, I don't think the defense played to their standard, but the offense had their backs. That is the thing with this team: we all have each other's backs. It is something special and something dangerous, especially in the playoffs." Saratoga fans cheer for their team during the Section 2 Class AA semifinals against Shaker on Friday in Saratoga Springs. (Jim Franco/Times Union) Key moment On a night where defense took a back seat to offensive efficiency, Georgeadis helped secure the Super Bowl berth with his interception. "That kid deserved that play by far," Morris said. "That kid is the definition of football in my head. I watch his film all the time. His life is football, football, football. What a play." Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Usman Khawaja’s new book makes a startling claim about the 2018 Cape Town scandal, popularly known as the "Sandpapergate." A 2021 joint statement from four leading Australian bowlers is now under scrutiny. Khawaja says he waited eight years for the truth to emerge before speaking himself. MORE: Sandpapergate at Cape Town, South Africa: Revisiting the ball-tampering scandal that rocked Australian cricket eight years back Did Australia’s bowlers know about Sandpaper Gate? The official line held that only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft had any knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball during the third Test against South Africa. item.title: Saint Louis fights off Mizzou to win Show Me Showdown
item.description: Saint Louis burst onto the scene last year with a 24-1 start to the season and an NCAA Tournament victory. Josh Schertz, the man behind the special 2024 Indiana State team, put together one of the most fun teams in the country last season and had a handful of returners. Everyone knew getting good opponents on the schedule was a challenge, but on Friday, the Billikens had an opportunity against an in-state rival in Missouri. With possibly their biggest game of the season staring them in the face, Schertz’s group didn’t blink. Saint Louis controlled the Show Me Showdown and beat Mizzou 90-84. Despite the game’s magnitude, Saint Louis was more than ready. “In these games, you got to believe you belong,” Schertz said. “You can’t look at yourself as some sort of ‘lesser than.’” The “Atlantic-10 Splash Bros” set the tone early for Saint Louis. After a 3-0 Mizzou start, Ishan Sharma buried a 3 that resulted in a four-point play. Trey Green hit a 3 before Mizzou head coach Dennis Gates could use his first timeout of the game. By the time Gates got his team over to talk, it was Saint Louis by eight. The hot start for the Billikens continued as they went into the halftime break shooting nearly 57% from the field and 56% from distance. Mizzou forward Bryson Tiller noted how good Saint Louis’ offense is. “With Sharma and Green, those [other] guys, they can really spread the floor,” Tiller said. “Michaeli can really drive it.” Saint Louis didn’t slow down in the second half, but did have to withstand multiple late Mizzou pushes. It was Alon Michaeli who sealed the game with a couple of key baskets and free throws in the final two minutes. “He had played a good game up until the final two minutes… but the scoring down the stretch was huge for us,” Schertz said. Saint Louis held Mizzou five-star freshman Jason Crowe Jr. to just 3-for-18 shooting from the field. Schertz credited Quentin Jones for his defense on Crowe Jr. throughout the game. “Amari (McCottry) and Kellen (Thames) were on the All-Defensive team, and I would make a case that Q is the best individual defender of all those guys,” Schertz said. As the final buzzer sounded, the Billikens and their fans were ecstatic. Over the summer, Trey Green and Ishan Sharma said that they had the Mizzou game circled. On Friday, Saint Louis proved that they were no one-year wonder. Even without Robbie Avila, who was barred from playing for Saint Louis on Friday by the College Sports Commission , Saint Louis was the better team against a high-major team with a ton of talent. “The best way to get what you want in your life is to deserve what you want in your life,” Schertz said.

item.description: EVANSVILLE — Memorial coach John Hurley was asked this week how many sectional championships he has won. He didn't know the number off hand, nor was it important. All of his attention and emphasis was on the next opportunity. Hurley, now in his 19th season at his alma mater, knows not to anticipate anything easy once the calendar turns to November. Just ask his undefeated teams the last two seasons. A singular pointed goal: extend the season another week. More: Southwestern Indiana high school football sectional finals updates, scores No. 1 Memorial defeated No. 8 Mater Dei 28-7 on Friday, Nov. 6 at Reitz Bowl to win the Class 3A sectional championship. Far from a masterpiece performance – too many penalties, for starters. The result was still the same. The Tigers (11-0) stood firm behind its defense in the second half to reach the regional round for the first time since 2023. "You get to this time of the year, anything can happen," Hurley said. "We're just going to keep grinding away at it. I'm just proud of the kids. I know what they've done to get to this point." No offensive explosion or head-turning sequence this week . Memorial was simply the tougher team. The defense limited the opponent to only 174 total yards – a miniscule 2.3 yards per carry when factoring in sacks. The only scoring drive for Mater Dei came in the first quarter after converting a fake punt. The Wildcats only ran around a dozen offensive plays after halftime. The major reasoning: the Tigers won every notable moment on defense. Kellan Carter forced a fumble midway through the third quarter. Rhylan Brogden made a fourth down stop. item.title: Mavericks’ Dusty May gives props to ‘winning player’ Morez Johnson Jr. for big game vs. Jazz
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Mavericks’ Dusty May gives props to ‘winning player’ Morez Johnson Jr. for big game vs. Jazz appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Dallas Mavericks dominated the struggling Utah Jazz en route to a 112-100 win in the NBA Cup. The game was a memorable one for Morez Johnson Jr., who had a breakout game as he notched the first double-double of his career with 13 points and 17 rebounds, including an impressive 10 offensive boards. Mavericks head coach Dusty May , who also coached Johnson when they were at Michigan, was full of praise for the rookie . May noted that after a slow start in part due to a lower leg injury during preseason, Johnson is getting back to his best physically. “The first glimpse was in San Antonio when Naji (Marshall) threw the lob, and ‘Rez went up and got it. Even though he didn’t finish it, that was the first glimpse when the staff said, ‘Okay, his athleticism is almost back,'” May said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) May also applauded the fact that Johnson can still put up big numbers despite not getting his number called on many plays. “His energy, his effort. He’s a winning player, and for a guy you don’t call any plays for, if you can get him 13 and 17 without calling any plays for him. We need those types of glue guys,” May added. Heading into the game, Johnson was averaging 7.4 points and 3.1 rebounds in eight games, all off the Mavs bench. But as his performance against Utah showed, the No. 9 pick in this year’s draft of capable of a lot more. His game figures to be a nice complement to Cooper Flagg, who has the skillset of a potential top-10 player . As Johnson continues to get back to peak fitness, he figures to provide some much-needed energy and physicality to the Mavs in the frontcourt. Saint Stephen’s 29, St. Edwards 6 The Falcons turned their relentless rushing attack and stingy defense into a 29-6 victory over the Pirates in an SSAA 11-man BOUND bracket quarterfinal game at the Moore Athletic Complex at Turner Fields. The next assignment for the Falcons (8-4) will be a semifinal game at home next Friday against Oxbridge Academy (9-3), whic defeated Glades Day, 22-21, in its quarterfinal game. The Pirates (7-5) jumped out to a 6-0 lead in the first quarter on an 11-yard TD pass from junior Dylan Colontrelle to sophomore Chase Colontrelle before the Falcons scored 29 unanswered points. The Saint Stephen’s defense slammed the door, forcing the Pirates to turn the ball over on downs four times in Saint Stephen’s territory, including three times inside the Falcons 10-yard line. “That was really frustrating,” Pirates head coach Rich Schofield said. “I felt like our defense was out there a ton. item.title: ONE Fight Night 49 MMA And Submission Grappling Results: Lee, Czaban, Hugo, And Israilov Shine In Bangkok
item.description: ONE Fight Night 49: Gabriel vs. Magomedov went down live in U.S. primetime from Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, on Friday, November 6, and the card’s MMA and submission grappling action kept the energy high from beginning to end. A heavyweight grappling trilogy between a pair of World Champions was settled in a flash, ending a rivalry nearly a decade in the making. Plus, two undefeated debutants squared off in a grinding bantamweight clash with a perfect record on the line, while an unbeaten rising star went the distance in a tightly contested atomweight chess match. Finally, a strawweight clash that opened with a grappling scare ended in a choke and could lead to a World Title opportunity. Here’s what happened in the MMA and submission grappling matches at ONE Fight Night 49. Lee Sinks In Rear-Naked Choke To Submit Lalthazuala View this post on Instagram “The Flash” Lee Seung Cheol may have just earned a crack at the ONE Strawweight MMA World Title. The South Korean handed Nazareth “The Northstar” Lalthazuala his first career loss, as he submitted the Indian phenom via rear-naked choke in the second round of a match that was filled with plot twists. Most of the opening frame was spent on the canvas, with Lalthazuala hunting for submissions and even getting close to securing a choke. The Indian MMA star looked like he’d be gliding toward an easy win. But Lee weathered the storm, and he returned more determined in the second stanza. The 27-year-old South Korean had his opponent trapped against the ropes and rained down ground-and-pound. Lalthazuala threw up-kicks until he could create enough space to stand, but the two soon went back to the mat and battled for position. Lee won that battle, as he took the back of the 25-year-old and sunk in the choke for the tap at the 3:04 mark of round two. That submission win moved Lee’s record to 14-1, put him on a 14-bout winning streak, and inched him closer to a shot at ONE Strawweight MMA World Champion Joshua Pacio , who will defend his belt at ONE SAMURAI 5 on November 18. item.title: LeBron James avoids 'depths of hell' from Cavs fans, but scoring scarce in loss
item.description: CLEVELAND — Akron native LeBron James still has the date on the tip of his tongue: Dec. 2, 2010. It's when James visited the Cavaliers for the first time as a member of the Miami Heat and experienced the wrath of enraged Cleveland fans who felt betrayed by "The Decision." Nearly 16 years later, James visited the Cavs (5-4) for the first time as a member of the Philadelphia 76ers (8-2) on Friday, Nov. 6, receiving loud cheers during player introductions and a mostly warm reception, albeit mixed with some booing, in the Cavs' 119-95 blowout victory . James said it was "great" how Cavs fans received him in his latest homecoming game. But was the 2003 St. Vincent-St. Mary High School graduate wondering how it would go after he left the Los Angeles Lakers this past summer and announced on July 24 he would sign with the 76ers in free agency instead of his other primary suitors, the Cavs, Heat, Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves? "I don't know because at the end of the day, nothing can get as worse as Dec. 2 2010, from a reception standpoint," James said. "So, I've seen damn near the depths of hell when it comes to reception here all the way to, like, the heavens above. So, anything in between is easy money." In a rare occurrence, scoring did not prove to be easy for the 41-year-old James. He finished with a season-low eight points on 3-of-12 shooting from the field (0 of 4 on 3-pointers), seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and six turnovers in 32 minutes. "Too many turnovers on my behalf, and I didn't feel in a rhythm offensively all day," James said. "... Every game has its own challenges, and I don't think [we played well] offensively as a group. And I know I damn sure wasn't good at all." Cavs news: How the Cavaliers spoiled LeBron James' most recent Cleveland homecoming game The NBA's all-time leading scorer, James has failed to reach double figures in scoring in just 10 regular-season games in his career. His streak of 396 consecutive regular-season games with double-digit scoring in Cleveland was snapped, according to ESPN. "The biggest thing is just making it tough [on James]," Cavs guard Donovan Mitchell said. "He's a hell of a player, but [we were] just trying to pack the paint and knowing that he's trying to drive to also kick. He had six turnovers, and you give credit where it's due to our defense as a whole. From there we were able to get out and get going." The Cavs avenged their 114-106 season-opening loss on Oct. 22, when Cleveland blew a 29-point lead during James' first home game in Philadelphia. In the rematch, Mitchell scored a game-high 23 points to go along with seven rebounds, eight assists and two steals. Forward Evan Mobley compiled 22 points, six rebounds, four assists, a steal and a blocked shot. item.title: Captain Shreve’s Gabe Lockett dials in dominating runs against Byrd
item.description: Byrd fans looking for a storybook ending to their otherwise disappointing season Friday night against archrival Captain Shreve instead came away licking their wounds at Lee Hedges Stadium. Powered by the undauntable legs of senior Gabe Lockett , the Gators rolled 48-21 in the 49th running of the Backyard Brawl, which annually pits neighbor against neighbor in one of the longest running rivalry games in Northwest Louisiana. Lockett rushed for 336 yards and 5 TDs with four of the scores and 212 of the yards coming in the first half, when the Gators (5-4) dominated the Jackets (1-9). Lockett averaged 14.6 yards per carry while delivering TDs on runs of 11, 4, 63, 38 and 60 yards. “I knew this was an important game because we needed a home game,” Lockett said. “Coming into the game I was dialed in and running hard. They couldn’t stop us. They couldn’t stop the run. Couldn’t stop the pass. I’m proud of my guys and we’re gonna go and do it next week.” MAXIMUM EFFORT: Byrd’s Maxie sets record in loss as Haughton, BTW, Northwood win PREDICTIONS: Top Shreveport-Bossier high football games in Week 10 predictions The game ends the season for Byrd, while the Gators will find out Sunday if they did enough to warrant a home LHSAA playoff game in the first round as expected. Shreve’s victory means the Gator seniors went 4-0 against the Jackets, which is a rarity in the series. The Shreve defense held record-setting Byrd running back Christian Maxie to just 127 yards and one late TD when the game was out of hand. The senior concludes his career with 4,577 yards, the most in school history. “That was our best collective effort defensively,” said Shreve coach Jeremy Wilburn, a former Byrd quarterback. “We were prepared from a scheme standpoint. I thought we had our guys in good positions to make plays and then they made those plays. We came back out at halftime and maintained that aggressive mentality on defense.” Byrd still leads in the series 29-20, but has lost its domination of the Gators. The Jackets had won 26 of the last 31 meetings with Shreve before the current run. “I think this group of seniors has understood the process a little more each year of how to prepare for a game like this and not let the moment be too big,” Wilburn said. “We had so many guys participate in such a productive way that it was truly a collective effort from all three phases. And we’re super proud of that.” Jimmy Watson covers Louisiana sports for the USA TODAY Network. Email him at jwatson@shreveporttimes.com and follow him on Twitter @JimmyWatson6. item.title: 'I'm never going to give up!' - Everton star Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall sends message to Thomas Tuchel with Coventry goal hours after England squad snub for Jobe Bellingham
item.description: FBL-ENG-PR-EVERTON-COVENTRY - AFP Everton midfielder Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall vowed to keep fighting for a maiden international call-up after scoring in Friday night's 3-1 Premier League victory over Coventry City. The 28-year-old found the net at Hill Dickinson Stadium just hours after England boss Thomas Tuchel overlooked him in favour of Jobe Bellingham. Midfielder responds on Merseyside pitch Dewsbury-Hall channelled his frustration into an emphatic display on Friday evening as his fierce strike helped Everton secure consecutive top-flight wins and climb to fifth in the table. Tipped to make the cut for this month's Nations League matches following a strong run of form, the playmaker learned earlier that day that Borussia Dortmund teenager Bellingham had been selected ahead of him . Even so, Tuchel acknowledged on Friday afternoon that the Toffees man had been "very close" to inclusion after enjoying "a very good season". Playmaker vows to keep fighting Reflecting on his omission while speaking to Sky Sports after the comeback triumph over Coventry, Dewsbury-Hall said: "It was a disappointing morning, I'm not going to lie. It's a massive dream of mine to play for my country. I know I was close. [I'm] sad, yeah, but really proud of myself and how I have reacted. All I can keep doing is putting in good performances and hopefully one day I get the nod, because I'm never going to give up." Tactical freedom sparks Merseyside revival Overcoming obstacles is nothing new for the midfielder, who had EFL loan spells at Blackpool and Luton Town before making his Premier League bow for boyhood club Leicester City at 22, suffering relegation and winning the Championship under Enzo Maresca. After following the Italian to Chelsea for £30 million and being largely restricted to cup outings during his sole campaign at Stamford Bridge, he joined Everton in summer 2025 and has since recorded 11 league goals and seven assists. Praising his current role on Merseyside, Dewsbury-Hall said: "I'm really, really enjoying it. I've got a really good hybrid role in this team, where the gaffer is giving me the freedom to pop up all over the pitch." Reiterating his international determination, he added: "I've got the mentality. I'll keep pushing and pushing and see what happens." March window offers next opportunity With the November international break now underway, Dewsbury-Hall faces a four-month wait until March for his next chance to earn an England call-up. Maintaining his clinical output across the winter schedule will be essential as he looks to keep Everton in contention for European qualification. Continuing to thrive in his free-roaming midfield role could finally force Tuchel's hand when the Three Lions reconvene in the spring.

item.description: Naugatuck's Qwentarvous Lee had a 68-yard touchdown pass and TD runs of 18 and 29 yards while finishing with 142 yards on 14 carries in a 41-14 win over Seymour on Friday, Nov. 6, 2026, at Naugatuck High School. (Roger Cleaveland/Hearst Connecticut Media) NAUGATUCK - Going into this high school football season, there was some uncertainty in Naugatuck as to how good the Greyhounds could be. Although the team had some offensive talent, coach Chris Anderson needed to see something more from his players. He wanted to see them play with heart, with conviction for one another and with an attitude befitting a champion. "Our team motto is, ‘Earn it,'" Anderson said. "Since Day 1, we have told them the only thing we are entitled to is the air we breathe. Everything else we have to go earn. We felt like we lost that a little bit last year. We had a little entitlement and issues like that. We wanted to get back to old-fashioned hard work, and ‘Earn it' has been our rally cry." That rallying cry could be heard loud and clear throughout Craig Peters Field on Friday night as the Greyhounds remained undefeated with a dominant 41-12 win over a very good Seymour team that had won five games in a row. Qwentarvous Lee scored two touchdowns and threw for another. Brandon Andoh rushed for a game-high 145 yards, scored two rushing touchdowns and caught a 68-yard touchdown pass, and the Naugatuck defense held a potent Wildcats offense in check to complete the total team effort. Seymour had scored 44 points or more in each game of its winning streak, but Naugatuck intercepted three passes and forced the Wildcats to turn the ball over on downs three times while the Greyhounds ran out to a 21-0 lead and cruised to their eighth win of the season without a loss. The Naugatuck defense set the tone early, as the Greyhounds stopped Seymour on a 4th-and-9 play at the Naugy 34-yard line on the Wildcats' first possession of the game. Then Naugy needed only five plays to score on a 57-yard pass play from Sean DiBona to Malachi Kinchen. Seymour drove deep into Naugatuck territory on its second possession, but again came away with nothing when Kinchen intercepted Max Brito's pass on fourth-and-8 from the Greyhounds' 18-yard line, creating a major momentum swing. Eric Harriott and MJ Delpino also intercepted passes for the Naugatuck defense, which was led by inside linebacker Josiah Loyd, Raily Hernandez and Isaiah Portalatin. "I can tell you that we have definitely improved on defense from the beginning of the season," Kinchen said. "Our defense looked a little shaky in the beginning of the season, but our coaches made adjustments and put players in spots they needed to be, and they made plays." Quarterback Max Brito led Seymour offensively with 77 yards on 17 carries, while Connor Shea finished with 58 yards on 11 carries. They each scored a touchdown. item.title: ‘Hands down’ – Rival NBA head coach makes strong Luka Doncic MVP claim
item.description: Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images Luka Doncic’s start to the season has been so good, even his opponents are giving him MVP shouts at this point. The Los Angeles Lakers are off to a 7-2 start through their first nine games. A lot of this is thanks to the absolutely incredible start that Luka Doncic is off to. The Slovenian superstar is averaging 38 points, eight rebounds, and eight assists a game while being extremely committed on the defensive end. Doncic has never won the NBA MVP award despite being in contention for it for half a decade. This season seems like it might be the one if he keeps going like this. And despite the fact that his Portland Trail Blazers have to face Luka on Friday, head coach Micah Nori has given him a huge compliment. Micah Nori says it is a ‘perfect offensive storm’ for Luka Doncic and that he’s currently the MVP The MVP is far from decided after just 10 games, Victor Wembanyama has been making quite the claim for himself in the early going as well. item.title: ‘Do y'all know?’: Stephen A. Smith shares the ‘wild thing’ he’s noticed about Kevin Durant lately
item.description: Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images Kevin Durant’s role may have changed with the Houston Rockets this season. The 38-year-old is one of the most efficient players in NBA history and has the ability to destroy teams by scoring 30 or 40 points in a game. However, this season, Durant has averaged around 20 points a game. Stephen A. Smith thinks he knows why. Stephen A. Smith hails Kevin Durant’s new role with the Houston Rockets Smith has watched Durant for a long, long time now. The First Take host knows everything the Rockets star is capable of, which is perhaps why he isn’t surprised by his points-per-game average this season. Smith believes Durant has taken a step back to allow those around him to shine, just so that he can save his energy and do what he does best in the latter stages of the season. He said on ESPN : “Let me say this about Kevin Durant while I’m here. I looked at his numbers the other day. Do y’all know that the 20 points that Kevin Durant is averaging, which is like his lowest in years, do y’all know why? “Kevin Durant has taken like 12 shots a game. And so I’m looking at it, and I’m like, now he deserves a lot of credit for that. That’s a wild thing because we all know what he can do. He shoots 53% from the field. He’s shooting more than 40% from three-point range. “Why is Kevin Durant averaging 20? Because he’s deferring to the other cats. Because he’s playing the long game. He knows what he’s going to need come what they’re going to need from him come April, May, and possibly June.” Smith further hailed Durant’s leadership and claimed that he could step up and score 30 or 40 points in a game whenever he feels like it. He said: “I’m looking at Houston the way KD is flowing. You know, at any time he wants to, he could drop 30 or 40. He could do that. “So, I’m looking at that and I’m saying testament to him, his greatness, his leadership, his willingness to step back and defer and help upgrade the cats around him. You’re a career 27-point-per-game scorer who’s one of the most efficient offensive superstars we’ve ever seen.” Durant has come under some criticism from fans and the media for not shooting enough this season, but if this is the reason why, he is right to do it. The Rockets are 7-2 so far this season and are among the favourites to go the distance. If Durant leads his team in the same way and then starts dominating games late on, Houston could well do it. item.title: St. John’s welcomes back former captain Sadiku Ibine Ayo in Sunday’s game versus Iona
item.description: Mar 22, 2026; San Diego, CA, USA; St. John's Red Storm head coach Rick Pitino talks with forward Sadiku Ibine Ayo (2) in the first half against the Kansas Jayhawks during a second round game of the men's 2026 NCAA Tournament at Viejas Arena. Mandatory Credit: Denis Poroy-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sunday’s game for St. John’s will be much more emotional than usual non-conference matchups. The Red Storm will welcome back former two-time captain Sadiku Ibine Ayo as he returns to Madison Square Garden with the Iona Gaels. Before this season, Ibine Ayo had known only one head coach in college basketball: Rick Pitino. He began his career playing for the Hall of Famer at Iona, then followed him to St. John’s when he was hired to lead the program in 2023. Now he’s back at the school where his college career began. It will be without Pitino this time. “He’s like a son to me. My children really joked around, saying, ‘How could you let one of your children get away?” Pitino said on Wednesday, “And that’s the way they looked at him, like a brother. And my grandkids call him Uncle Sadiku.” After injuries cut his sophomore year short, Ibine Ayo served as a team captain for both of the Red Storm’s Big East championship squads the last two seasons. While his on-court contributions were minor, he was vital in establishing the Red Storm’s winning identity. Ibine Ayo effectively relayed Pitino’s coaching philosophy to his teammates and provided an example in practice with his work ethic and physicality. “Sadiku is invaluable in the locker room, invaluable in practice,” Pitino stated. “He just makes sure everybody does it the right way. He’s going to make sure that everybody understands what the coaches are all about and what the culture is all about.” Unlike many transfer portal moves, there was clear and honest communication between Ibine Ayo and Pitino when the forward left the program. Pitino said Ibine Ayo took less money to play with Iona, and he believed that was the right decision for him. “I was totally in favor of it. He needs to play major minutes,” Pitino told the media. The Johnnies head coach also knew, like himself, that Ibine Ayo was a New Yorker at heart, and he was going to stay close to home when choosing his next stop. After Ibine Ayo decided to return to Iona, the head coach told him he’ll be at some of his games in New Rochelle. Another Red Storm member looking forward to seeing Ibine Ayo again is Ian Jackson, who knew him since they were classmates at Our Savior Lutheran High School and described him as a brother. “That’s my guy, man, I hope he does great there,” Jackson said on Wednesday. Ibine Ayo has started in Iona’s first two games of this season, going scoreless in their season opener against Vermont, then putting up 10 points and five rebounds versus NJIT on Thursday night; both games were wins for the Gaels.

item.title: Why 76ers star Joel Embiid still believes in his outside shot amid 3-point shooting slump

Even so, the Sixers star insists he has not lost faith in himself. Embiid went 0-of-9 from the field in Friday’s 119-95 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers, including 0-of-2 from beyond the arc. That dropped him to just 3-of-28 from 3-point range on the season, according to ESPN’s Dave McMenamin. He shot 33.3% from deep last season, and head coach Nick Nurse has encouraged him in the past to take more threes , not fewer. The shooting woes have become a running theme for Embiid early in the season. Just two nights earlier, he went 0-of-3 from deep in a win over the Detroit Pistons and joked afterward that it “might’ve been the last three I ever take.” He still found ways to contribute in that one, posting 26 points and 15 rebounds. Friday was a rough night for Philadelphia as a whole, as the Sixers never led by more than two points. The Sixers shot 36.5% from the field and 25% from 3-point range, while LeBron James struggled in his return to Cleveland with eight points on 3-of-12 shooting and six turnovers. VJ Edgecombe led the way with 19 points, and Tyrese Maxey added 17. Donovan Mitchell paced the Cavs with 23 points, while Evan Mobley chipped in 22. The loss snapped Philadelphia’s five-game winning streak and dropped the team to 8-2. Embiid and the Sixers will look to bounce back when they visit the Chicago Bulls on Sunday. item.title: Lakers’ Luka Doncic calls out NBA mentor: ‘He don’t even call’
item.description: Luka Doncic kept it real ahead of Friday’s game between the Lakers and Trail Blazers. The Western Conference matchup streamed on Amazon Prime, where Doncic’s mentor and friend Dirk Nowitzki is a part of the NBA crew’s studio show. The former NBA champion sang the superstar’s praises ahead of the matchup, and Doncic was asked if he had anything to say to Nowitzki. “He don’t even call. He’s in LA and he don’t even call no more, so I expect that dinner soon,” Doncic said. “I expect that call.” Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers reacts to a call during the game against the Portland Trail Blazers at Crypto.com Arena on November 06, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Getty Images Of course, Doncic was playfully calling out his friend, who has been a longtime supporter of the guard since he was with the Mavericks. Doncic and Nowitzki were franchise stars in Dallas, but the former never got his happy ending with the organization. Instead, the Mavericks shockingly traded Doncic to the Lakers in February 2025. The blockbuster deal stunned the league and essentially kick-started a new era in Los Angeles. Dirk Nowitzki attends the NBA On Prime Season 2 Launch Event “The Art Of Basketball” at Storied NYC on October 13, 2026 in New York City. Getty Images for Prime Video Now, Doncic is officially the Lakers leader as the team has opened the 2026-27 season as one of the top teams in the West. While the 27-year-old is evidently preoccupied with the Purple-and-Gold, he hasn’t forgotten about his longtime mentor. Nowitzki was asked about Doncic’s pregame comments during the Amazon Prime NBA halftime show, where he laughed at the Lakers superstar’s cheeky answer. Luka Doncic of the Los Angeles Lakers celebrates during a game against the Miami Heat at Crypto.Com Arena in Los Angeles on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. NBAE via Getty Images “I’m big time now,” Nowitzki joked.
